source.title: Abstention is not Refusal, But It Affects Safety of Large Language Models
source.citation: Abstention is not Refusal, But It Aff…

page_placements.theme: Refusal direction vs directions for other non-answering behaviours (abstention, hedging, incapability, bail, derailing, privacy refusal): overlap and specificity

record.tranche_reason: The study derives a harmful-minus-benign refusal direction and intervenes on it, measuring non-refusal on harmful prompts. Its steering setup and evaluation are not the full all-layer projection ablation and set of measures specified by the claim.
record.gate_note: The safety results for reverse steering along vref and its projection-removed residuals are recorded. The positive-vref result on harmless TriviaQA questions reports response-frame shares, not a refusal rate, so it is not a behavioral refusal row. Abstention induction/suppression on ordinary question-answering benchmarks is not recorded because it does not measure refusal to harmful user requests. Results cited from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study builds a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction (vref, following Arditi et al.) and reports non-refusal rates on held-out harmful AdvBench prompts under reverse steering, against an unsteered baseline and a random-direction control. This bears directly on V1's 'removing the direction removes refusal' part, using a different intervention: single-layer activation subtraction at all token positions rather than all-layer projection ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that epistemic abstention and safety refusal are geometrically and behaviourally distinct (cosine 0.25–0.68, distinct response frames) but not interventionally independent: reverse steering the benign-derived abstention direction breaks refusal. Projection removal weakens this effect in Qwen3.5 and Gemma3 but not in LLaMA3.1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means refusal direction and activation steering, but intervenes at one selected layer per model rather than projecting the direction out of every layer; evaluates validity-gated non-refusal on held-out AdvBench.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect of projection removal varies by model: it substantially weakens the abstention-direction effect in Qwen-3.5 and Gemma-3 but does not detectably weaken it in LLaMA-3.1. The relative effect of −vabs versus −vref also varies by model. A single selected intervention layer is used per model.

fits_no_version.finding: Reverse steering along an abstention direction derived only from benign answerable/unanswerable contrasts breaks refusal on harmful prompts (.72–1.00). Removing its projection onto vref weakens this to .40–.64 in four models but not in LLaMA-3.1 (.87).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directions for other non-answering behaviours, derived from benign data, can suppress safety refusal, and this is only partly explained by their linear overlap with the refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction with its abstention-direction component removed (vref⊥abs) still breaks refusal, at .24–.79 versus .76–.98 for the full vref.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Part of the refusal direction's causal effect on harmful prompts is shared with an epistemic-abstention component.

record.problems: The refusal-direction intervention is performed at one selected layer rather than by all-layer projection ablation. The study does not measure general capability costs. Its random-direction control uses one sampled direction per model and does not estimate variability across random directions. The validity gate can exclude malformed outputs; the authors report that it lowers rates only for LLaMA's vabs-derived arms. WildGuard's refusal field uses a broader definition than the stricter human criterion and is reported to conservatively under-count broken refusals.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant table rows were left out. Abstention-benchmark steering results, positive-steering response-frame shares, and calibration-only sweeps were not extracted as claim rows because they do not report refusal rates on harmful or harmless requests.

untested.parts: Projection ablation at every layer (only single-layer subtraction is tested). Rate of refusal induced by adding vref to harmless prompts (only response-frame shares and examples are given). Preservation of general capabilities (not measured).
No jailbreak-suppression analysis and no adversarial training.
There is no test of multiple refusal directions or cones. The vref⊥abs residual still breaks refusal, but this is not framed or analysed as a multi-direction test.
Qwen3.5's thinking channel is disabled, and the authors exclude reasoning models.

missing.what: Positive steering with +vref on answerable TriviaQA questions yields almost entirely safety-framed responses (0.96–1.00 of valid abstaining responses), with example refusals. No refusal rate is given, so V1's addition part cannot be quantified; a row with state cannot_determine could record it.

record.verdict_notes: The study's focus is abstention; vref serves as a comparator that replicates the refusal-direction effect by single-layer subtraction. Non-refusal is validity-gated WildGuard refusal, which the authors report as conservative relative to stricter human labels. Qwen3.5 was run with thinking disabled.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests reverse steering along a difference-in-means safety-refusal direction at one selected layer per model, not projection ablation at every layer. It does not quantify whether adding vref makes the models refuse harmless requests, nor test whether general capabilities remain intact.
No test of attacks that suppress vref or training against its ablation.
The comparison is between an abstention direction and a refusal direction; it does not test whether refusal itself is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
The study reports refusal and response-harmfulness evaluations but does not test whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
No transfer test of the safety-refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or training stages.
No reasoning-model test; the paper explicitly notes that its models and setup do not address reasoning models.

relation.reason: Its own −vref results (Table 8: .76–.98 non-refusal from .01–.05 baselines, random .01–.11) bear directly on whether removing the direction removes refusal, though vref is a comparator to the paper's main abstention direction.

tranche.reason: Builds the Arditi-style harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means vref but removes refusal by negative activation addition at one layer instead of all-layer projection. It reports non-refusal rates against an unsteered baseline and a random control. This is a different method on the same question.

source_check.notes: The pack lists the one V1 verdict without an [lN] id, so label_id 'l1' is a placeholder. r06 holds the −vabs value (.88) instead of −vref (.84), and r11's baseline repeats it. Layer ℓ* and |α| were calibrated for abstention induction, not for vref. There is no capability check, and the random control is one direction per model. The LLM-judge prompt in Appendix C.1 is quoted method text, not an instruction to the reader.

statements.correction: Table 8 random-control non-refusal: LLaMA-3.1 .07, Qwen3.5 .01, Gemma3 .09, Qwen2.5 .11, Gemma2 .03. −vref: .84, .98, .76, .83, .96. Gap −vref minus random: .67–.97 (median .77). Gap −vref minus baseline: .72–.97 (median .78). One independently sampled random direction per model, same norm and magnitude. The authors say it does not estimate variability across random directions.
statements.problem: The random-control range .01–.11 is right and so is filing the study under 'specific', but the '+0.506 median gap' is not in the text and matches no gap computable from Table 8. Also there is one sampled random direction per model, not several.

statements.correction: This study removes refusal by reverse activation steering (−vref, difference-in-means AdvBench minus Alpaca) at one layer ℓ* (13/18/23/18/20) at all token positions, not by all-layer projection or a weight edit. Controls: unsteered baseline and one random direction. No capability check.
statements.problem: Makes no specific claim about this study (no rows cited). If the study is counted among V1 supports framed as 'removal by all-layer projection or the equivalent weight edit', that misdescribes its method.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reverse steering along the extracted refusal direction on held-out AdvBench prompts across the five tested instruct models
reader_labels.reason: Non-refusal rises from low unsteered baselines to .76–.98 under −vref, while the random-direction controls remain near baseline (r01-r10, r16-r20). This supports a causal effect of steering along the direction, but not the full all-layer ablation or harmless-request addition claim.
